clue.text: Another way to speak of camp Liberal fleeing through back road

parts.note: to back a proposal is to second it

indicators.note: one piece passing through another sits inside it, so the shortened camp goes within the back road

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road

indicators.note: the Liberal fleeing means his letter runs out of the camp's name

parts.note: a gulag is a Soviet labour camp

explanation.surface: A remark about the camp style of a Liberal politician escaping down a back road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camp' looks like an adjective for the Liberal, but it is a noun, the Soviet labour camp; 'fleeing' drops the L and 'through' puts what remains inside the back road.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue learnt after one's mother tongue is a further way of speaking.

clue.text: Ryan Giggs let loose in striking fashion

indicators.note: letters let loose are freed from their order and fall into a new one

explanation.surface: The Welsh footballer Ryan Giggs is unleashed and plays brilliantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let' looks like part of the indicator 'let loose', but it is fodder: RYANGIGGSLET has the twelve letters needed, and 'loose' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggering means astonishing, so doing something staggeringly is doing it in a strikingly impressive way.

clue.text: It gets drunk secretary to hold up bit of lingerie

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece holding another up sits below it, so the secretary goes under the lingerie

parts.note: a cup is part of a bra
PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

explanation.surface: Something gets drunk while a secretary holds up a scrap of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea, something one drinks.

clue.text: English innocent has nothing on in the shade in Africa

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece placed on another sits above it, so the zero comes first

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero
green means naive, inexperienced

explanation.surface: An innocent Englishman, wearing nothing, rests in the shade somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a colour, a 'shade', with 'in Africa' pointing to the river that names it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nile green is a pale bluish-green colour named after the African river.

clue.text: Lion oddly rears primates

indicators.note: oddly picks the first and third letters of the word lion

parts.note: to rear up is to rise

explanation.surface: A lion behaves strangely by rearing up on its hind legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorises are small nocturnal primates of south and south-east Asia.

clue.text: Character in the Iliad with light sort of weapons

parts.note: the Iliad is written in Greek, and nu is a Greek letter, a character
clear means light, bright

explanation.surface: A figure from Homer's epic is armed with light weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' looks like a hero of the poem, but it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear weapons are a class of arms powered by atomic fission or fusion.

clue.text: Fifth group of soldiers to join up

parts.note: a unit is a body of troops
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The fifth company of soldiers is ordered to link up.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to combine or come together as one.

clue.text: It's Goethe's novel, so be very discriminating!

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving I, T and S
the possessive 's is no letter, leaving the poet's name

explanation.surface: A remark that a book by the German writer Goethe is a sign of real discernment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the noun for a Goethe book, but it signals the anagram; 'discriminating' is meant in its harsh sense of segregating.
explanation.definitionFit: To ghettoise a group is to confine it to a segregated area, an act of extreme discrimination.

clue.text: Dismay of the Pope with head of Anglicans advancing

indicators.note: the letter advances to the front of the word meaning of the Pope

parts.note: papal means of or relating to the Pope

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Anglicans are dismayed by a papal move with their leader moving forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of Anglicans is the second A of PAPAL, which moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to fill them with horror or dismay.

clue.text: Caught cheat swapping sides

indicators.note: the two ends of the word for a cheat, its sides, change places

parts.note: a deceiver is a cheat

explanation.surface: A cheat is caught out as he defects to the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping sides' swaps the first and last letters, D and R, of DECEIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To have received a ball, or a cold, is to have caught it.

clue.text: Player on the wings fit and well when the Reds struggled in Europe

definitions.text: when the Reds struggled in Europe

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two outer letters

parts.note: an ague is a fit of shivering fever
a spring is a well, a source of water

explanation.surface: A winger who is fit and well when Liverpool had a poor European campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a red-shirted football club; the Reds are the Communists, whose 1968 reforms in Czechoslovakia were crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prague Spring of 1968 was a period of reform in Communist Czechoslovakia, ended by Soviet invasion.

clue.text: 27 fruit farms

indicators.note: the answer to 27 across read as an instruction says put good, G, in place of nothing, O

parts.note: oranges are fruit

explanation.surface: A cross-reference that pretends some worthless fruit comes from the farms.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 across is GOOD-FOR-NOTHING, read as G (good) replacing O (nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a farm with its farmhouse and outbuildings.

clue.text: Eastern churchman, one making a cross

parts.note: a lector reads lessons in church

explanation.surface: An Orthodox cleric is someone who makes the sign of the cross.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests crossing oneself; the cross is the X a voter marks on a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter marks a ballot paper with an X, so one making a cross is a voter.

clue.text: German runner, man clutching hip after run

indicators.note: the clutching man comes after the letter for run

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: one piece clutching another holds it within

parts.note: he stands for a man
in means fashionable, hip

explanation.surface: A German sprinter clutches his hip after a race.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'runner' in crosswords is often a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a river flowing through Germany, and rivers run.

clue.text: Like compilers noticing anagrams with cry of surprise

indicators.note: making anagrams of a word rearranges its letters

parts.note: O is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Crossword setters, noticing anagrams, cry out in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters such as Picaroon work under pseudonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Setters' identities are hidden behind pen names, so they work in disguise.

clue.text: Society making waves in prioritising economy

parts.note: crimping hair is pressing it into waves

explanation.surface: A society causing a stir by putting economy first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making waves' suggests causing trouble, but it is the hairdressing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrimping means being very sparing with money, putting saving first.

clue.text: Rogue's pile spanning rolling acres

indicators.note: the money spans the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a mint is a pile of money

indicators.note: rolling letters tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A villain's estate takes in acres of rolling countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pile' suggests a stately home, but here it is a heap of money; the 's of Rogue's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer, a villain or rascal.

clue.text: Collar film actor from the east taking lead in movie that's dubbed

parts.note: to collar a criminal is to nick him

indicators.note: the turned actor takes in the other piece
in an across answer reading from the east is right to left

parts.note: James Dean was a Hollywood film actor

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Arresting a film star from the east who plays the lead in a dubbed movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' turns DEAN into NAED, which takes in M.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nicknamed has been given a familiar name, dubbed.

clue.text: He produces some art when playing

definitions.text: He produces some art when playing

indicators.note: playing with letters moves them around

explanation.surface: A virtuoso makes art while performing.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a great musician or conductor, whose playing is art.

clue.text: What's on TV? Nothing showing is to prove very compelling

parts.note: TV is short for transvestite, who wears drag
O is zero, nothing
on means being shown

explanation.surface: Is nothing on the television worth watching?
explanation.walkthrough: 'TV' looks like television; it stands for transvestite.
explanation.definitionFit: To dragoon is to force someone by coercion, to compel them.

clue.text: Take legal action about journalist's material

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way

parts.note: ED is an editor, a journalist; the 's is no letter

explanation.surface: Suing over a reporter's article.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is a soft napped leather used as a material.

clue.text: What's to drag and heave heading for Europe?

definitions.text: What's to drag and heave heading for Europe?

parts.note: to lug is to drag
to gag is to heave, retch

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: What does a traveller haul about on the way to the Continent?
explanation.definitionFit: Bags and cases are what a traveller hauls on a journey abroad.

clue.text: Did express almost derail unexpectedly?

indicators.note: the letters fall out in an unexpected order
almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Was the express train nearly derailed out of the blue?
explanation.walkthrough: 'express' suggests a train; it is a verb. 'almost' leaves DERAI.
explanation.definitionFit: To have aired one's views is to have expressed them.

clue.text: Transport has vents with it

parts.note: to vent an opinion is to air it
with it means fashionable, hip

explanation.surface: A vehicle has air vents fitted.
explanation.definitionFit: An airship is a powered lighter-than-air craft, a means of transport.

clue.text: Country's bowler perhaps taking single before India

indicators.note: in a down answer the hat piece comes before, above, the letter for India
the hat takes in a letter

parts.note: a bowler is a kind of hat
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
I is India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A nation's cricket bowler takes one wicket before facing India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket; it is the hat. The 's of Country's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a Caribbean nation on the island of Hispaniola.

clue.text: Plug for Harry Potter — billions in turnover for book

indicators.note: turned over means read backwards
a plug sits inside a hole, so these words are what is held within the following words

explanation.surface: A commercial for the boy wizard brings in billions in sales.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading backwards through 'Potter billions' gives the answer; 'turnover' looks like sales revenue.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the text, or book, of an opera or musical.

clue.text: Perhaps Clegg gets in great excuse

indicators.note: one piece gets in another, inside it

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, great, written with I for the figure one
Nick Clegg led the Liberal Democrats, so he is an example of a Lib

explanation.surface: The former deputy prime minister has a superb pretext.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a plea of being elsewhere, an excuse.

clue.text: Feckless Democrat pursues sentimentality of the very cheapest kind

indicators.note: the abbreviation for Democrat follows the sentiment

parts.note: goo is sickly sentimentality
something cheapest of all comes for nothing, free

explanation.surface: A hopeless politician follows the most worthless kind of sentiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A good-for-nothing person is idle and useless, lacking any purpose.
